search_text: published ZDI-10-127 ZDI-CAN-737 Ipswitch Imail Server Mailing List Remote Code Execution Vulnerability 2010-07-15 9.0 ['Ipswitch'] ['IMail'] This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable installations of IPSwitch IMail. Authentication might be required to exploit this vulnerability. The specific flaw exists within imailsrv.exe which is invoked to handle messages sent to the imailsrv. When a message subject contains a "?Q?" operator the string following that sequence is copied to a local stack buffer. No validation of the data or data length is done. In order to reach this code path a mailing list must be password protected (authentication required) or have previously had a password configured (no authentication required). A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code under the context of the SYSTEM user. Update to the latest version 11.02 ['2010-06-08 - Vulnerability reported to vendor', '2010-07-15 - Coordinated public release of advisory'] Anonymous https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-10-127/
title: Ipswitch Imail Server Mailing List Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
vulnerability_details: This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable installations of IPSwitch IMail. In order to reach this code path a mailing list must be password protected (authentication required) or have previously had a password configured (no authentication required). A remote attacker can exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code under the context of the SYSTEM user.
